2318.title: [Feature]: Geometry-aware dispatch to stop the recurring "silent AABB" bug class
2318.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I have searched the issues and discussions and found no similar feature request.

### Feature Description

**What:** A small geometry-aware dispatch layer so detection ops use the geometry each detection actually carries (mask / OBB / box) instead of silently falling back to the axis-aligned `xyxy`.

**Why:** Several recent fixes are the same bug in different functions: code grabs `detections.xyxy` and forgets the real geometry lives in `data["xyxyxyxy"]` (OBB) or `mask`. Because `xyxy` is always present, the wrong answer is the silent default:
- `Detections.area` returned the AABB area, not the rotated body (#2306)
- `with_nms` / `with_nmm` dropped crossed OBBs via AABB IoU (#2303)
- `as_yolo` dropped OBB rotation on export (#2289)
- `roboflow/inference`: consensus IoU, and stitch / crop corner shifts (https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2420, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2427, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2430)

Same root cause each time: `Detections` holds several geometries at once and `xyxy` is just a derived envelope, so every consumer re-implements "which geometry is the real one?" and forgetting it fails silently. The next geometry-aware function will hit it again.

**How:** Centralize the dispatch into a few batched helpers and route call sites through them instead of reaching for `xyxy`. No data-model change, keeps the vectorized design, backward compatible. Migration can be incremental, then deprecate the ad-hoc paths.

Proposed helpers (batched, no per-detection loops):
- `detection_iou(a, b)`: dispatches mask / OBB / box IoU
- `detection_area(det)`: mask sum / shoelace / box area
- `move_detections(det, offset)`: shifts `xyxy`, `mask`, OBB corners and keypoints together (what #2427 / #2430 each forgot)
- a `test_op_respects_geometry` contract test that fails when an op can't tell an OBB from its envelope

Rollout can be incremental and each step is independent / backward compatible: (1) consolidate the duplicated `move_detections` (pure dedup, no behavior change), (2) the read-only `detection_iou` / `detection_area` dispatch, (3) the contract test.

A first pass suggests more call sites in the same class worth investigating: `get_anchors_coordinates` (and therefore `LineZone` / `PolygonZone`) reads anchors off the envelope rather than the rotated body, `as_coco` and `as_pascal_voc` have no `is_obb` option and drop the rotation on export, `with_nmm` merges to the union envelope while keeping one input's `data["xyxyxyxy"]`, and `DetectionsSmoother` averages `xyxy` without smoothing the oriented corners.

### Example Usage

```python
# one dispatch per op, instead of every function re-deriving it
def detection_area(det):
    if det.mask is not None:        return det.mask.sum(axis=(1, 2))
    if "xyxyxyxy" in det.data:      return _shoelace(det.data["xyxyxyxy"])
    return box_area(det.xyxy)

# same shape for detection_iou (mask / OBB / box), plus a geometry-complete
# m

2757.title: [Bug]: DetectionDataset.as_yolo splits one object into several instances and exports COCO crowd regions as objects
2757.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I have searched the issues and discussions and found no similar bug report.

### Bug

#2702 fixed holes in 0.31.0; this issue is about multi-part objects and `iscrowd`, which are unchanged in 0.31.0. Related: #1209, where a maintainer said multiple polygons in one annotation should load as a single mask (loading now does this, but `as_yolo` splits the mask again on export), and #373, where disjoint masks were noted as unsupported.

When a COCO dataset is loaded with `from_coco(..., force_masks=True)` and saved with `as_yolo`, every external contour of a mask becomes its own YOLO line. An object made of two polygons (for example a person cut by an occluder) becomes two objects. COCO crowd regions (`iscrowd: 1`) are kept as ordinary objects, although COCO evaluation treats them as ignore regions. Nothing is logged in either case.

On COCO val2017 this changes the instance count of the YOLO export, and a model trained or evaluated on the export sees extra small objects and crowd blobs as positives.

**Output of the example below:**

0 0.05000 0.40000 0.05000 0.49000 0.34000 0.49000 0.34000 0.40000

**Expected:**
- One line per annotation. YOLO segmentation has no multi-polygon form, so the parts need to be joined (Ultralytics' `merge_multi_segment` does this) or, at least, the split should be logged.
- Crowd regions skipped by default or behind an option, with a warning either way.

1388.title: Create new cookbook for utilizing supervision methods to easily create YOLO datasets for training
1388.body:
### Search before asking

- [X] I have searched the Supervision [issues](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/issues) and found no similar feature requests.


### Description

I find myself creating dataset structures and split in train, valid, test and images, labels folders multiple times. The whole process could easily be automated.

### Use case

There are methods that currently exist to load a dataset `sv.DetectionDataset.from_yolo()`, split in selected ratio `sv.DetectionDataset.split()` and export to YOLO format `sv.DetectionDataset.to_yolo()`.

Nevertheless, in creation of YOLO model training dataset structure, someone must write a custom split in train/valid/test (because `split()` is able to split only in two parts), and also create manually the train/valid/test folders needed for the preparation of the dataset. (As of my knowledge ultralytics YOLO models require by default to have train/valid folders that contain valid and not empty annotations, test folder can be empty).

 For that reason I propose a new method to be added in `sv.DetectionDataset` which will combine the arguments of `from_yolo(), split(), to_yolo()` and will run the whole backend for creating train/valid/test folder and images/labels subfolders along with data.yaml file.

At this current point I have developed an implementation of such method which provides the ability to the user to create a YOLO dataset structure with a single line of code. An example of executing such a process can be seen in the following example:

```
import supervision as sv

dataset_directory = "/path/to/directory"

sv.DetectionDataset.create_yolo_dataset(
    images_directory_path=f"{dataset_directory}/images",
    annotations_directory_path=f"{dataset_directory}/labels",
    data_yaml_path=f"{dataset_directory}/data.yaml",
    train_ratio=0.7,
    valid_ratio=0.15,
    folders_export_path=f"{dataset_directory}",
    data_yaml_export_path = f"{dataset_directory}/data.yaml",
)
```

### Additional

- The `test_ratio` is automatically calculated based on the `train_ratio, valid_ratio`.
- The arguments provided in the example are all mandatory arguments to be passed.
- The user can provide any additional optional argument incorporated in `from_yolo(), split(), to_yolo()`.

Let me know if you like this idea, and if you want to submit a PR with the initial implementation.

2702.title: [Bug]: DetectionDataset.as_yolo / as_pascal_voc / as_labelme write a mask with a hole as two instances
2702.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I have searched the issues and discussions and found no similar bug report.

### Bug

**What's the bug?**
A mask that contains a hole (for example a ring, or any SAM mask with an interior gap) is exported as two
instances of the same class: one for the outer contour and one for the hole.
sv.mask_to_polygons uses cv2 RETR_TREE and discards the hierarchy, so hole contours come back as ordinary
polygons, and approximate_mask_with_polygons passes them straight to the writers.

**Expected behavior:**
One instance per mask. as_coco already handles this (it uses RLE for masks with holes).

**Actual behavior:**
as_yolo writes two label lines, as_pascal_voc two <object> elements and as_labelme two shapes. Reloading the
YOLO export gives two instances with areas [2500, 480] instead of one instance of 2100 px (the outer polygon
is also filled, so the hole is lost). as_createml never writes masks, so it is not affected.

**Error/Traceback (if any):**
```python
# No error: the export succeeds but writes the wrong labels.
```

### Environment

- Supervision: 0.31.0.dev0 (develop @ 69cb843)
- Python: 3.11
- OS: macOS 15 (arm64)

### Minimal Reproducible Example

```python
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import supervision as sv

m = np.zeros((100, 150), bool)
m[10:60, 10:60] = True
m[25:45, 25:45] = False  # a hole; mask area is 2100

root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
(root / "images").mkdir()
p = str(root / "images" / "a.png")
Image.fromarray(np.zeros((100, 150, 3), np.uint8)).save(p)

det = sv.Detections(xyxy=np.array([[10, 10, 59, 59]], float), mask=m[None], class_id=np.array([0]))
ds = sv.DetectionDataset(classes=["ring"], images=[p], annotations={p: det})
ds.as_yolo(str(root / "y/images"), str(root / "y/labels"), str(root / "y/data.yaml"))

r = sv.DetectionDataset.from_yolo(

d = next(iter(r.annotations.values()))

2747.title: [Bug]: `as_pascal_voc` truncates fractional box corners instead of rounding them
2747.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I have searched the issues and discussions and found no similar bug report.

### Bug

`DetectionDataset.as_pascal_voc` writes `<bndbox>` corners with `str(int(x))` (`src/supervision/dataset/formats/pascal_voc.py`, `object_to_pascal_voc`), which truncates instead of rounding. A fractional box loses up to a full pixel at every corner. `[10.9, 10.9, 20.9, 20.9]` is written as `11 11 21 21` (1-indexed) instead of `12 12 22 22`.

The common case is a YOLO → VOC conversion. `from_yolo` reads normalized 6-decimal labels back as floats a hair off the integer pixel, so truncation moves whole corners. With the integer box `[0, 0, 37, 29]` on a 640×480 image, written by Ultralytics as `0 0.028906 0.030208 0.057813 0.060417`:

- `from_yolo` gives `[-0.00032, -0.00024, 37.0, 28.99992]`
- `as_pascal_voc` writes `xmin=0 ymin=0 xmax=38 ymax=29`. `xmin=0` is outside 1-indexed VOC, and `ymax` lost a pixel.
- `from_pascal_voc` reads that back as `[-1, -1, 37, 28]`

**Expected:** each corner goes to the nearest integer pixel, `xmin=1 ymin=1 xmax=38 ymax=30`, which reads back as `[0, 0, 37, 29]`. The loader in the same module already keeps decimals (#2568), so the writer is the only lossy step.

### Environment

- supervision `develop` @ 927dfeb05 (0.31.0)
- macOS arm64, Python 3.12.13, NumPy 2.3.1

### Minimal Reproducible Example

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv
from supervision.dataset.formats.pascal_voc import object_to_pascal_voc

elem = object_to_pascal_voc(np.array([10.9, 10.9, 20.9, 20.9]), name="cat")
print([elem.find(f"bndbox/{t}").text for t in ("xmin", "ymin", "xmax", "ymax")])
# ['11', '11', '21', '21']   expected ['12', '12', '22', '22']
```

2756.title: [Bug]: as_pascal_voc adds 1 to xmax and ymax; the VOC devkit needs the +1 on xmin and ymin only (complements #2747)
2756.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I have searched the issues and discussions and found no similar bug report.

### Bug

#2747 (with PR #2748) covers the `int()` truncation in the same function; this issue is about the remaining part, the +1 on xmax and ymax, which #2748 keeps.

`dataset/formats/pascal_voc.py` (line 72 in 0.30.9 and 0.31.0) adds 1 to all four coordinates before writing, citing #144 ("Pascal VOC coordinates are 1-indexed"). In the VOC devkit convention, pixel indices are 1-based and **inclusive**: a box covering 0-based pixels x0 .. x0+w-1 is written `xmin = x0 + 1`, `xmax = x0 + w`, so a box with `xmin=1, xmax=W` covers the whole image. Only xmin and ymin need the +1. Adding it to xmax and ymax makes every exported box one pixel wider and taller for readers that follow the devkit, such as Detectron2's `pascal_voc.py` loader, which subtracts 1 from xmin and ymin only.

supervision's reader subtracts 1 from all four coordinates (`xyxy_arr -= 1`), so a supervision -> supervision round trip looks exact, and the problem only appears when another tool reads the files. Reader and writer would need to change together.

This also affects #2747: with PR #2748, the 0-based box `[0, 0, 37, 29]` is written as `1 1 38 30`, but its devkit encoding is `1 1 37 29`. Integer boxes, which rounding does not change, are all one pixel too large on the right and bottom.

In our audit of COCO val2017 read with the devkit convention, 30% of the boxes exported by `as_pascal_voc` had IoU below 0.9 with their source box, most of them small objects; both the truncation and the +1 on xmax/ymax contribute, and #2748 removes only the first.

**Output of the example below:** `<xmin>11</xmin> <ymin>21</ymin> <xmax>41</xmax> <ymax>61</ymax>`. The devkit encoding of COCO box x=10, y=20, w=30, h=40 is 11, 21, 40, 60.

**Expected:** add 1 to xmin and ymin only when writing, and subtract 1 from xmin and ymin only when reading. Since #2748 is already changing this function, it may be simplest to fold the change into it. If the current behaviour is kept for compatibility with existing supervision files, a note in the docs would help.

Found while auditing COCO converters for a study of annotation-format conversion (preprint to follow). Happy to open a PR.

2544.title: [Bug]: from_pascal_voc fails on images with no objects since 0.28.0
2544.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I have searched the issues and discussions and found no similar bug report.

### Bug

**What's the bug?**

`DetectionDataset.from_pascal_voc` fails as soon as the dataset contains an image with no objects in it. A Pascal VOC XML file with a `<size>` block but no `<object>` entries is perfectly normal (it is how negative images are stored), but loading a directory that contains one raises an error and the whole dataset is lost.

The library's own exporter writes exactly this kind of file. `as_pascal_voc` on a dataset with an empty `Detections` produces an XML with no `<object>`, and `from_pascal_voc` then refuses to read it back, so the export and import are no longer a round trip.

This worked in 0.27.0 and earlier. It has been broken since 0.28.0 and is still broken on `develop`.

**Where it comes from**

In `src/supervision/dataset/formats/pascal_voc.py`, `detections_from_xml_obj` builds `class_id` like this:

```python
class_id = np.array(
    [extended_classes.index(class_name) for class_name in class_names]
)
```

When there are no objects, `class_names` is empty and `np.array([])` has dtype `float64` rather than an integer dtype. The `Detections` object itself accepts that, but `DetectionDataset.__init__` does not:

2288.title: [Bug]: `DetectionDataset.as_yolo` silently drops OBB rotation
2288.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I have searched the issues and discussions and found no similar bug report.

### Bug

`DetectionDataset.from_yolo` has an `is_obb=True` flag but `DetectionDataset.as_yolo` does not. The save path silently drops the OBB rotation and writes axis-aligned bbox lines instead.

`from_yolo(is_obb=True)` parses the 9-token OBB lines correctly and stores the four corners in `detections.data["xyxyxyxy"]`. But `detections_to_yolo_annotations` only loops over `xyxy` and `mask` - it never reads `xyxyxyxy`:

https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/blob/0c67942d32a650eee0ae13ec123587256ace3903/src/supervision/dataset/formats/yolo.py#L251-L290

So after a typical `from_yolo -> split -> as_yolo` flow, the saved labels contain 5 tokens per line instead of 9, and training a YOLO-OBB model on them just sees axis-aligned boxes.

Re-loading the saved file with `is_obb=True` also crashes the validator, since the loader expects 9 tokens and finds 5:

```
ValueError: First dimension of np.ndarray for key 'xyxyxyxy' must have size 1
```

Expected: `as_yolo` accepts `is_obb=True` and serializes the corners from `data["xyxyxyxy"]` as 9-token OBB lines.

Actual: no `is_obb` parameter; OBB corners are dropped on save.


### Environment

- Supervision: `0.29.0.dev`
- Python: 3.12.13
- OS: macOS 26.3

### Minimal Reproducible Example

```python
import os, tempfile, numpy as np, cv2
import supervision as sv

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    img_dir = os.path.join(tmp, "imgs"); os.makedirs(img_dir)
    lbl_dir = os.path.join(tmp, "labels"); os.makedirs(lbl_dir)
    cv2.imwrite(os.path.join(img_dir, "i.jpg"), np.zeros((100, 100, 3), np.uint8))

    # Rotated rhombus - not axis-aligned
    with open(os.path.join(lbl_dir, "i.txt"), "w") as f:
        f.write("0 0.5 0.1 0.9 0.5 0.5 0.9 0.1 0.5\n")
    with open(os.path.join(tmp, "data.yaml"), "w") as f:
        f.write("names: ['thing']\nnc: 1\n")

    ds = sv.DetectionDataset.from_yolo(
        images_directory_path=img_dir,
        annotations_directory_path=lbl_dir,
        data_yaml_path=os.path.join(tmp, "data.yaml"),
        is_obb=True,
    )

    out = os.path.join(tmp, "out_labels"); os.makedirs(out)
    out_yaml = os.path.join(tmp, "out.yaml")
    ds.as_yolo(annotations_directory_path=out, data_yaml_path=out_yaml)

    with open(os.path.join(out, "i.txt")) as f:
        print("Saved:  ", f.read().strip())
    # Saved:   0 0.50000 0.50000 0.80000 0.80000     5 tokens, rotation gone
    # Original: 0 0.5 0.1 0.9 0.5 0.5 0.9 0.1 0.5   9 tokens

    # Re-loading the saved file with is_obb=True crashes:
    sv.DetectionDataset.from_yolo(
        images_directory_path=img_dir,
        annotations_directory_path=out,
        data_yaml_path=out_yaml,
        is_obb=True,
    )
    # ValueError: First dimension of np.ndarray for key 'xyxyxyxy' must have size 1
```

285.title: Wrong COCO format while exporting a `sv.DetectionDataset` using its `as_coco` method
285.body:
### The Issue:
I export some annotations using:
 ```python
sv.DetectionDataset(
    classes=CLASSES,
    images=images,
    annotations=annotations
).as_coco(
    annotations_path=ANNOTATIONS_PATH,
    min_image_area_percentage=0,
    max_image_area_percentage=1.,
    approximation_percentage=0
)
```
The resulting `.json` is created successfully. 
Then, loading the annotations using `pycocotools` and plotting annotations of an image:
```python
from pycocotools.coco import COCO
coco=COCO(ANNOTATIONS_PATH)

imgId = 42  # an arbitrary image id
file_name = coco.loadImgs(imgId)[0]["file_name"]

img = plt.imread(file_name)
plt.imshow(img)
plt.axis("off")

annIds = coco.getAnnIds(imgIds=imgId, iscrowd=None)
anns = coco.loadAnns(annIds)
coco.showAnns(anns, draw_bbox=True)
```
which plots wrong annotations for the given `imgId`: the annotations (box & mask) is seen bottom-right and it seems that there is a mismatch between the image and its annotations. 
![image](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/assets/40141130/2b277d28-7487-49cf-a624-11b31f6e508b)

Actually, for any `imgId`, we have the same issue: the image is shown correctly but the annotations are not. Interestingly, the annotations (`annIds`) are always the same for different `imgId`'s. In my case, there is only 1 box & mask per image and for various values of `imgId`, the `annIds` are always equal to `1`.

### The Cause:
The `annIds` are not unique among all the annotations (the "id" in "annotations" in COCO format). 
I presume they have to be unique among all annotation id's ([see the following issue](https://github.com/cocodataset/cocoapi/issues/95#issuecomment-448038572)). 

However, the current implementation resets the ***annotation id*** to 1 for each image:
https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/blob/4f79d29934ebfbb59d4cb789b70e8e451f545332/supervision/dataset/formats/coco.py#L202


### The (possible) Fix:
Simply changing `label_id` to `annotation_id` in the following line will assign a unique id for each annotation:
https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/blob/4f79d29934ebfbb59d4cb789b70e8e451f545332/supervision/dataset/formats/coco.py#L218

I would be glad to open a PR.
